Gboard Clipboard History, Editing Tools and Patch Flags

Learn how clipboard retention experiments, editing shortcuts and Gboard Patches features differ from stock keyboard behavior.

What you should know

Clipboard content is potentially sensitive. Differentiate stock Gboard options from extra features added by Gboard Patches.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What stock and patched builds offer

Stock Gboard provides clipboard and text editing tools, while Gboard Patches documents enhancements to retention time, item count, preview formatting, backup/restore and a local-network web clipboard. These patched features are not proof that the same UI exists in every Gboard release. A flag that begins with pref_ may be a stored preference exposed by a patch.

The flags tell different stories

enable_extended_clipboard_history describes expanded historical behavior; pref_clipboard_ttl_ms refers to a retention period, not a Boolean. pref_force_cursor_trackpad_mode concerns editing navigation rather than clipboard storage. Data persistence, UI presentation and cursor movement should be tested independently.

Privacy before convenience

Clipboard histories may contain verification codes, private messages or financial text. Shorter retention can reduce exposure, while a web clipboard introduces LAN pairing and access considerations. The patch project documents controls, but the safest behavior depends on your configuration; don't expose a web clipboard without understanding how it authenticates and which network it can reach.

Frequently asked questions

Is pref_clipboard_ttl_ms an on/off switch?

Its name suggests a millisecond value; always inspect actual type before editing.

Is web clipboard built into every Gboard?

No. The cited Gboard Patches project adds its own web clipboard feature.
